messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: HIGH - host-gpu-12.redwood-prod - kernel panic detected; kubelet NotReady. Alert link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Incident PD12345 fired for service: gpu-host-monitoring. Initial trigger: serial-console kernel OOPS and heartbeat lost.

sara_oncall: acked on pagerduty. I’m on it, starting serial console attach.

mike_infra: thx. quick note — this host is in us-west1-rack4, dedicated pool for low-latency workloads. If we lose it we should auto-failover to host-gpu-12b.

sara_oncall: serial console attached. seeing repeated panic trace: 
```
[  345.123456] kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
[  345.123458] CPU: 3 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/3 Not tainted 5.15.0-rc1 #1
[  345.123460] Hardware name: AcmeServerXYZ, BIOS 1.2.3
```

sara_oncall: ssh attempts are timing out. I can’t access kubelet. metrics show node lost heartbeat at 14:02:11 UTC.

jenna_devex: tagging this as potentially customer-facing. Which routes are on that node? Any pinned model shards?

mike_infra: 3 pods were pinned to GPU: model-inference-prod-12, batched-gen-8, embeddings-hot-1. We have replicas in other racks, but traffic split was 60/40 so some requests will hit the remaining replicas and see higher latency.

ops_bot: Automated action: rerouting 30% traffic away from us-west1-rack4 to us-west1-rack2. Health checks for host-gpu-12 marked FAILED. :gear:

lee_sre: I’m taking over the on-call. @sara_oncall please handoff current state and what you’ve tried.

sara_oncall: Handoff: attached serial console, confirmed kernel panic logs (above), SSH unreachable, kubelet NotReady, pods still listed as Unknown on the node, attempted `kubectl drain host-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` but drain hung because kubelet unresponsive. Commands tried: 
```
# kubectl get nodes host-gpu-12 -o wide
NAME           STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
host-gpu-12    NotReady   <none>   120d v1.25.4

# kubectl describe node host-gpu-12
Kubelet last heartbeat: 2025-08-04T14:02:11Z
```

lee_sre: ok. next steps: cordon the node so scheduler stops placing new pods, then force-evict pods via API. Also open serial console log to infra to try a controlled powercycle.

mike_infra: I’m on the powercycle now — request raised to colo. ETA ~4 minutes. If the node reboots cleanly and kernel panic persists we’ll RMA the NIC/MB.

jenna_devex: customers to notify? Any SLAs impacted?

lee_sre: minimal customer impact expected but we should notify customers using the low-latency pool. Telemetry: 95th latency for text-generation rose from 220ms -> 310ms in the last 5 minutes and error rate on embeddings API +3.9%. Tagging two mid-market tenants that were pinned to that region.

ops_bot: Automated: started replacement host provisioning host-gpu-12-repl in us-west1-rack2; estimated ready in 7 mins. Scaling dedicated-pool +1 replica.

pagerduty: Escalation rule secondary reached (10m) because kubelet still NotReady; notifying infra lead.

mike_infra: colo confirms powercycle completed. Serial console shows POST then immediate panic again: 
```
Uptime: 0 days, 00:00:18
[   18.234567] kernel BUG at drivers/nv/gpu.c:1234
[   18.234569] Oops: kernel access of bad memory address in GPU driver
```

lee_sre: kernel panic repeating on boot -> hardware/driver likely. Taking node out of rotation permanently. @ops_bot ensure no traffic sent to this host. Start RMA flow.

ops_bot: Marked host-gpu-12 as "decommissioning" and rebalanced pods. Live log: `kubectl cordon host-gpu-12` -> `kubectl delete node host-gpu-12` after pods evicted. Rebalancing started.

sara_oncall: Verified that critical deployments have healthy replicas: 
- model-inference-prod: 4/4 healthy across other hosts
- embeddings-hot: 3/3 healthy

jenna_devex: customer impact summary for comms team: "We experienced degradation for a subset of low-latency requests in us-west1 for ~12 minutes while we failed over traffic from a host with a hardware/kernel panic. No data was lost; we are provisioning a replacement host and issuing an RMA for the faulty machine."

lee_sre: Good. Action items: 
1) RMA host-gpu-12 (mike)
2) Run a job to scrub core dumps if any were captured and attach to the ticket (sara)
3) Add test to preflight to detect this GPU driver regression (ops)
4) Postmortem in #postmortems within 48h (lee)

mike_infra: RMA ticket created INC-RMA-8893. Serial console logs attached.

sara_oncall: Found core dump on attached nvme: `/var/crash/gpu-core-2335007777.dmp` — uploading to S3 now. Upload link: https://s3.example/redwood/cores/gpu-core-2335007777.dmp

ops_bot: Replacement host host-gpu-12-repl ready and joined the cluster. Auto-scheduler started moving pods. Health checks green.

pagerduty: Incident PD12345 resolved (manual). Acknowledged by lee_sre. Duration: ~25m.

lee_sre: Closing notes: brief outage window ~25m, small latency bump while rebalancing. No customers escalated to support. Follow-up: investigate GPU driver release 525.x regressions; consider kernel lockstep testing on staging.

jenna_devex: I'll draft status update for customers and ops playbook changes.

sara_oncall: handing off to follow-up owners. I’m going offline for the next ticket. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
